The continuous-test dual is Jψ(μ)=sup_v(Eψ(v)−∫v dμ), with μ(T)=V. Constants cancel because E(u+c)=E(u)+Vc. Changing the actual continuous reference changes the dual by a finite constant.

notes.summary: Independent positive-curvature rational interpolation on finite graphs, including irrational cycles, loops and signed starting curvature. Dirichlet kernels and maximum-support calculus are reconstructed. No graph distribution is recognized as an actual metric.
notes.detailedSummary: Approximates shared vertex values in a nonzero divisible value subgroup and inserts upward rational-slope bends at value-group locations. Old positive margins survive, inserted curvature is positive, raw mass is preserved and potentials and measures converge. Proves cyclic-core kernel symmetry, branch-extension monotonicity and the diffuse maximum-support lemma. Exact execution covers only 140 interpolation and 210 raw-mass cases.
notes.text:
Mathematical graph theorem. Let Λ⊂R be a nonzero divisible additive subgroup, G a finite connected compact metric graph with edge lengths ℓ_e∈Λ and positive weights w_e, θ a signed vertex measure of mass V>0, and μ a nonnegative vertex measure of mass V. Fix a vertex z. Use Δ equal to the weighted sum of outgoing slopes. Then the anchored edge-affine solution F(z)=0, θ+ΔF=μ exists uniquely and is uniformly approximated by refined rational-slope functions H whose vertex values belong to Λ and whose complete curvature θ+ΔH is positive. Their curvature measures converge weakly to μ.

Proof. Subdivide each self-loop once at ℓ/2∈Λ, assigning zero starting and target mass to the new vertex. The one-vertex/no-edge case is F=H=0 with θ=μ=Vδ_z. Otherwise direct edge cancellation gives −Σ_v f(v)Δf(v)=Σ_{e=ab}w_e(f(b)−f(a))²/ℓ_e. Polarization proves symmetry; connectivity makes the kernel precisely the constants. The image is the zero-sum vectors, so anchoring gives existence and uniqueness.

After loop subdivision let k be the vertex count and ρ=(V/k)Σ_vδ_v. For 0<ε<1, με=(1−ε)μ+ερ has strictly positive mass at every vertex. The anchored solution Fε depends linearly on its right-hand side and converges, with every original edge slope, to F.

Λ is dense because it contains Qa for any nonzero a∈Λ. Approximate the finitely many shared values Fε(v) by g_v∈Λ with error at most h and g_z=0. On an oriented edge a→b set d=g_b−g_a and c=d/ℓ. Choose rational q1<c<q2, each within η/2 of c, and choose 2h/min_eℓ_e<η/2. Insert a bend at t=(d−q2ℓ)/(q1−q2). Strict bracketing gives 0<t<ℓ; divisibility gives t∈Λ. Put slope q1 before t and q2 afterwards. The terminal value is exactly g_b and the inserted value g_a+q1t belongs to Λ. Shared endpoint values therefore agree around every cycle.

At the bend the curvature is w_e(q2−q1)>0. The initial and terminal edge contributions are w_eq1 and −w_eq2, so their sum together with the bend is zero. Every old outgoing slope changes by less than η. Choose ηΣ_{e incident v}w_e<με(v)/2 at each old vertex; its curvature remains strictly positive. Total mass is exactly V. The edgewise uniform error against Fε is at most h+ηℓ_e, while total inserted mass is less than ηΣ_ew_e. Let approximation errors and ε tend to zero along a diagonal sequence. This proves uniform potential convergence and weak curvature convergence. A common integer clears the finitely many rational slopes and preserves all Λ-valued vertices, yielding integral Λ-affine approximants after denominator clearing.

The fixed-edge alternative genuinely fails: on two parallel edges of lengths 1 and √2, shared difference d and rational slopes force d∈Q∩√2Q={0}. The inserted bends remove this obstruction. For θ=(1,1), μ=(2,0), ε=1/10, the difference is d=(9/10)(2−√2). Slopes .52,.53 and .37,.38 give interior bends at −127+90√2 and −180+128√2. Old masses are 189/100 and 9/100, and each bend has mass 1/100; total mass is 2.

Finite-core kernel proof. For unweighted G, define j_z(x,y) by Δ_xj_z=δ_z−δ_y and j_z(z,y)=0, subdividing at x,y,z as needed. The same anchored matrix supplies existence and uniqueness. With D(f,h)=Σ_e∫f′h′=−∫fΔh, integration by parts gives D(j_z(·,x),j_z(·,y))=j_z(x,y)=j_z(y,x). A negative minimum cannot occur at z, contradicts the negative sink at y, and otherwise propagates through zero slopes to z or y; hence j_z≥0. The maximum is attained at y. Summing outgoing currents across a regular level between zero and the maximum gives total current one; each crossing current is nonnegative. Consequently every edge slope has absolute value at most one. Symmetry gives |j_z(x,y)−j_z(x,y′)|≤d_G(y,y′), and joint continuity follows.

If G′ adds trees to G and r collapses them, then j_z^{G′}(x,y)=j_z^G(rx,ry)+λ(x,y), where λ is the common initial root-path length when x,y lie in the same attached tree, and zero otherwise. Outgoing slopes at the attachment vertex and along the trees give the same source, sink and anchor; uniqueness proves the formula. Thus old kernels are preserved and retracted kernels increase as branches are added. Loops remain in the core. Weighted branches would require resistance lengths ℓ/w; subsequent curve applications use unweighted split skeleta.

Maximum-support lemma. If a kernel potential h satisfies Δh=α−σ for positive equal-mass Radon measures and σ is supported on a nonempty finite set S, then max_Gh=max_Sh. Kernel estimates make h Lipschitz with edge derivatives of bounded variation. Set M=max_Sh and b=(h−M)^+. Edgewise Stieltjes integration and vertex cancellation give Σ_e∫|b′|²=−∫bΔh=−∫b dα≤0, since b vanishes on S. Thus b is constant on connected G and zero on S. Polygonal uniform/Sobolev approximation also justifies the integration identity. This is graph calculus, not a claim that a Thuillier lisse function is CLD smooth.

Execution observations. graph_checks.py uses exact Q(√2) arithmetic and passed all assertions in 140 specified interpolation cases and 210 raw-mass/energy cases. The grids include signed starting curvature, unequal weights, a subdivided self-loop, cyclic cores and added branches; kernel symmetry, branch-extension and the singleton case passed. The largest slope-grid denominator used was 512. These results are exhaustive only for those generated finite grids and establish no analytic, formal or psh assertion. Program/output: graph_checks.py, graph-checks-output.json and graph-checks.stdout.txt. Rerun: python3 graph_checks.py.

notes.detailedSummary: Under explicit actual-model, skeleton and local-frame antecedents, constructs genuine continuous atoms, solves diffuse retracted targets by uniform convex averages and bounds the decreasing endpoint's extended energy before invoking O. Weighted symmetry and local analytic section norms establish all-point uniqueness. A finite continuous orbit average and a maximum-support proof verify N downstairs before D transfers the equation. Higher-dimensional original requirements remain open.
notes.text:
This theorem is an implication relative to n1 and n2, with additional unverified geometric antecedents. It is not an unconditional all-genus result.

R1: Over complete algebraically closed nontrivially valued C, the smooth connected projective curve X and actual ample rational L possess a finite semistable core Σ0 with type-II vertices and lengths in Λ=−log|C*|, and an actual projective rational bundle model ψ0 whose component-degree measure θ has raw mass V=deg L.

R2: Finite skeleta containing Σ0 form a directed system of continuous compatible retractions r_G:T→G separating all analytic points. Enlargements subdivide edges and add trees; every type-II and type-III point belongs to a finite graph. Complementary branches are actual analytic open balls with the stated disk topology. Type-II subdivisions have value-group lengths.

R3: Every rational-slope, Λ-valued PA f on such a value-group graph with θ_G+Δf≥0 is realized on a refined actual projective rational model of the same bundle. Its additive metric is ψ0+f∘r_G, its component degrees and genuine continuous MA coefficients are exactly θ_G+Δf, and nef recognition supplies actual fixed-bundle FS approximation. New contracted components have starting degree zero. This actual global realization is an assumption, not a consequence of n2.

R4: On complementary formal-fibre balls a local analytic frame of a cleared power of L has constant ψ0 norm; core-factoring corrections retain it. Nested finite disk ancestors converge to each terminal point and actual analytic section norms decrease under disk inclusion.

R5, for the downstairs intrinsic criterion: the completed-closure carrier has a nonempty finite Galois orbit S of actual type-II points. A finite-extension semistable model with split components is a prospective source, not verified here. No fixed point on a graph with loops is assumed.

Conditional atom construction. Choose a type-II core vertex z. Solve θ+ΔFz=Vδ_z with Fz(z)=0. By n2 and R3 its positive rational approximants are actual continuous psh metrics on the actual bundle. Uniform closure and genuine continuous MA continuity give ψz=ψ0+Fz∘r_Σ0 with MA(ψz)=Vδ_z. On a larger graph, Fy=Fz−Vj_z(·,y) satisfies θ_G+ΔFy=Vδ_y. The same construction gives the actual continuous scalar ay=−Vj_z(·,y), ay(z)=0, MA(ay)=Vδ_y for type-II y. Type-III y follow by type-II approximation along an edge, kernel Lipschitz continuity and genuine uniform MA continuity. This avoids applying n2 to type-III edge lengths outside Λ. The branch formula makes these global kernels independent of the chosen graph.

Weighted symmetry and norming. O's curve energy identity against ψz is E(p)=½∫p MA(p)+(V/2)p(z). Expand it on (1−t)p+tq and compare the derivative at zero with O's ∫(q−p)MA(p). This gives ∫p MA(q)−∫q MA(p)=V(p(z)−q(z)). O makes all integrals finite and makes p(z),q(z) finite through the output Vδ_z; no pole subtraction occurs. For continuous psh p normalized by p(z)=0, testing q=ay gives p(y)=−∫j_z(x,y)dMA(p)(x)≤0.

The real algebra generated by continuous finite-retraction pullbacks separates points by R2. Stone–Weierstrass gives uniform density in C(T); every fixed algebra element is unchanged by all sufficiently large retractions. Hence r_Gx→x against all continuous functions and finite graph points are dense. Continuity gives sup_Tp=p(z). For a decreasing actual FS endpoint, the stage maxima are its values at z. Their limit is finite unless the endpoint is identically −∞; passing pointwise gives sup p=p(z). Thus ψz satisfies the actual N hypothesis, and N now proves all-E1 integrability iff finite continuous dual over C. Reference covariance allows any other continuous psh reference.

Arbitrary-support existence. Let μ be a positive Radon measure of mass V and finite dual relative to ψz; put ν=μ/V and μ_G=(r_G)*μ. Define j_G(x,t)=j_z^G(r_Gx,r_Gt) and u_G(x)=−V∫_G j_z(r_Gx,y)d((r_G)*ν)(y). Partition the compact finite graph into Borel pieces of small diameter. Their probabilities give finite convex averages of the actual ay, and the kernel Lipschitz estimate controls uniform error. Actual convexity/uniform closure gives continuous psh u_G; curvature affinity on a curve and genuine uniform continuity give MA(u_G)=μ_G, including diffuse edge measures.

Finite-retraction algebra tests are fixed by sufficiently large graphs. Uniform density and common raw mass imply μ_G→μ weakly along the directed system. No countable cofinal family or single skeleton replaces the support. The branch formula makes j_G increase and u_G decrease, with u_G(z)=0. For I_G=∫∫j_G dν dν, ordinary bounded-kernel Fubini yields E(u_G)=−V²I_G/2, ∫u_G dμ=−V²I_G, and E(u_G)−∫u_G dμ=V²I_G/2. These are raw constants, not probability-normalized energy formulas.

Every u_G is a genuine continuous dual competitor, so E(u_G)≥−J(μ). Actual decreasing closure gives an all-point psh endpoint u, anchored at zero. O's extended decreasing-energy continuity applies before E1 membership and proves E(u)=inf_GE(u_G)≥−J(μ)>−∞. Only then may O's endpoint operator law be used: MA(u)=lim_GMA(u_G)=μ. No arbitrary-net measurable MCT or abstract-Hilbert-to-actual completion is invoked.

Every-solution uniqueness. For any actual E1 solution p normalized at z, weighted symmetry against ay gives p(y)=−∫j_z(x,y)dμ(x) at every type-II and type-III point. O's atom-test integrability ensures these values are finite. At a terminal point x in a complementary ball, R4 gives a cleared-power frame with constant ψz norm. Each section of an FS system is analytic in that frame. Its Gauss norms decrease on nested closed disks, and its terminal norm is bounded by all ancestor norms. Real weights, finite maxima and decreasing actual FS nets preserve this monotonicity. For finite ancestors y_i→x, p(y_i) decreases to ℓ≥p(x). Upper semicontinuity gives p(x)≥limsup_i p(y_i)=ℓ. Thus p(x)=ℓ, including −∞. The same argument covers radius-zero type-I and nested empty-intersection type-IV terminals. All solutions therefore agree modulo one finite constant at every point, without subtracting common negative infinities.

Variational statement. O's concavity and segment derivative at a solution give E(v)−E(u)≤∫(v−u)dμ for every actual E1 v. Thus u attains the supremum. Decreasing continuous majorants converge in energy and in their integrals against the fixed output by O's weighted law. Hence J(μ)=V²sup_GI_G/2, E(u)=−V²sup_GI_G/2 and ∫u dμ=−V²sup_GI_G. O supplies necessity of intrinsic integrability for outputs; the verified norming reference permits N to identify it with finite dual. C supplies strict locality and comparison. This direct construction replaces the need for a normalized-family compactness/envelope/outer-derivative argument in this conditional curve proof; those properties are not separately asserted in the full original domain.

Finite-orbit norming and descent. Under R5, construct every continuous actual atom metric φ_y, y∈S, normalized by sup(φ_y−ψ_C)=0 against an invariant pulled-back reference. Semilinear equivariance and the already proved every-solution uniqueness identify g*φ_y=φ_{g^{-1}y}. The finite continuous convex average φ_S is actual psh and invariant, with curvature (V/|S|)Σ_Sδ_y. D descends it; O pushes its curvature to Vδ_ξ because all orbit points have quotient image ξ. There is no field-degree factor.

Invariance alone does not prove norming. For a continuous psh scalar h against φ_S, let α=MA(φ_S+h) and σ=(V/|S|)Σ_Sδ_y. Weighted atom representations show that on every finite graph containing core and S, Δ(h|_G)=α_G−σ. The maximum-support lemma of n2 gives max_Gh=max_Sh. Density gives sup_Yh=max_Sh. A downstairs scalar has equal values on S, so every downstairs FS scalar has supremum h(ξ); decreasing endpoints extend the equality. Only now is N applied downstairs.

For finite J_K targets, D gives the unique invariant lift of raw mass V and equal finite upstairs dual. The actual upstairs construction supplies a solution. Supremum normalization, equivariance and every-solution uniqueness make it invariant. D descends the actual singular metric and identifies extended energies before downstairs E1 membership; O pushes its genuine MA to μ. Any other downstairs solution pulls back to an actual E1 solution whose invariant output must equal that unique invariant lift. Upstairs uniqueness and surjectivity give every-point equality downstairs. No singular or noninvariant test is averaged. T covers trivial fields.

R1–R5 have not all been discharged. Consequently this is a complete conditional argument, not an unconditional all-genus theorem and not original P16.4 closure. The full proof is retained in P16.4-argument.md and P16.4-paper.tex.

notes.text:
The attempted actual bridge starts with a pure FS metric on the actual bundle. BE Theorem 5.14 supplies its semiample projective rational model in its stated domain. A strictly semistable dominating model and value-group refinements are then required. After clearing denominators, n2's approximants are integral Λ-affine; GH B.7 constructs a vertical Cartier divisor on the refined formal model by value-group constants times integral node monomials, with overlap ratios units. Tensoring that divisor with the old model of mL preserves the actual bundle.

The sign is checked independently. For the canonical generic section 1 of the vertical line bundle, let F=−log‖1‖=mH. KRZB gives 0=div(F)+Σ_vdeg(O(D)|C_v)δ_v. Its graph divisor is the negative sum of outgoing slopes, so component-degree correction is +Δ(mH). The tensor bundle therefore has degrees m(θ+ΔH), positive at all refined vertices. On a reduced one-dimensional special fibre these degrees imply nefness. A single-point skeleton is handled separately: its degree is V and constants have zero correction. KRZB Theorem 2.6 excludes that skeleton and cannot be invoked unchanged.

At an inserted node coordinate t=val(b), with original xy=π, local admissible blowup charts are xv=b, y=(π/b)v and uy=π/b, x=bu. The subedge lengths are t and val(π)−t. These equations verify the local subdivision, not global gluing, formal line-bundle algebraization, projectivity or domination over a non-Noetherian valuation ring. Once an actual projective nef rational model exists, BE Theorem 7.8/Corollary 7.9 recognize its metric using actual ample-model perturbations and FS approximation. GM Proposition 4.11/Lemma 4.12 provide an algebraic ample-domination route; they do not recognize an abstract graph or an unalgebraized formal bundle.
